name: Jungle Green
lede: Jungle green is a modern name for a cool green; the name's definition and this swatch do not quite agree.

sections.title: What the name means
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *jungle green* as a deep yellowy green, a dark or blackish green [1]. The swatch shown here is far lighter and bluer, a bright sea-like green whose nearest ISCC-NBS name is simply light green [2]. A competing swatch in our library, from the xkcd color survey, is a darker green, #048243 [2]. So the name covers a range of colors [1][2].

The Maerz and Paul dictionary of 1930 dates the name to 1926 [2]. The books say nothing more, and no history is claimed [1]. Neighbors include [[sea-green]], [[kelly-green]] and [[forest-green]], all in the family of [[green]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Jungle green is almost absent from painting. Only 1 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive holds a color near this swatch, as photographed [3]. In printed English the word peaks in the 1950s and rose fastest in the 1940s, though it also names the landscape, so the curve can mislead [4].

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, "jungle green"
